relationships.name: Complementary Colors
relationships.description: Colors that sit directly opposite each other on the wheel, creating strong contrast and visual energy.

relationships.name: Analogous Colors
relationships.description: Colors that sit next to each other on the wheel. They are naturally harmonious and feel calm when used together.

relationships.name: Triadic Colors
relationships.description: Three colors evenly spaced around the wheel. They balance contrast and harmony when saturation is controlled.

relationships.name: Split Complementary
relationships.description: A base color plus the two neighbors of its complementary color, giving contrast with less tension than pure complementary.

theoryCards.title: Primary Colors
theoryCards.summary: Red, yellow and blue are the traditional primary colors in art.
theoryCards.details: They cannot be created by mixing other pigments in subtractive systems and act as the base for many palettes.

theoryCards.title: Secondary Colors
theoryCards.summary: Green, orange and violet are created by mixing pairs of primaries.
theoryCards.details: They sit between the primaries on the wheel and often appear in vibrant, energetic palettes.

theoryCards.title: Analogous Schemes
theoryCards.summary: Analogous schemes use neighbors on the wheel for smooth transitions.
theoryCards.details: They are ideal for backgrounds, gradients and calm interfaces where softness is more important than contrast.

theoryCards.title: Complementary Schemes
theoryCards.summary: Complementary schemes pair opposites, like blue and orange.
theoryCards.details: They create high contrast and are powerful for call-to-action buttons and accents, but should be balanced with neutrals.
